rule_summary: A foster care provider (pleegzorgaanbieder) may only sign a foster care contract (pleegcontract) with a foster carer who is at least 21.
notes: The Youth Act (Jeugdwet) sets the same conditions for carers of a child they know (netwerkpleegzorg) and of a child they do not know (bestandspleegzorg).

rule_summary: There is no maximum age. Age matters more for long-term care of children under 4, and less for part-time and crisis care.
notes: Pleegzorg.nl is run by the providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland.

rule_summary: Providers may treat the age gap as an extra criterion. The starting point is that the carer ideally does not reach state pension age before the child turns 18.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 4
notes: For care by family or friends, a placement in the child's own network comes before the size of the age gap. For crisis care, an older age can help. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Single people and couples of the same or different sex can foster, with or without children of their own. The same steps and conditions apply to grandparents, other relatives and friends.
notes: The national government page says the same: it does not matter whether you are married or single.

rule_summary: Foster carers can come from every background, culture and faith. Providers pay attention to the cultural, ethnic and religious background of the child, the parents and the carers when matching.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 10
notes: Pleegzorg.nl also says foster carers come from all backgrounds, cultures and faiths. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: The law sets no income requirement. A provider may add criteria of its own, for example on the family's financial situation, if it writes them down and tells applicants in time.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, sections 4 and 5
notes: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: No teaching or care qualification is needed, and no large house. What you need is room in your life and the will to be there for a child.
Work can be combined with fostering. Part-time care fits a job well; long-term care makes working a lot harder. People on some unemployment or sickness benefits can also foster.
notes: Self-employed foster carers have no right to a leave benefit.

rule_summary: Employees who take in a foster child or an adopted child have a right to up to 6 weeks of leave, with a benefit from the employee insurance agency (UWV). The leave can start 4 weeks before the child arrives and must end within 22 weeks after.
notes: For foster care leave the child must be registered at the carer's address; for adoption leave the court must have granted the adoption. Not given as a value because weeks is not an allowed unit.

rule_summary: A medical statement is not required. Health is discussed during home visits. If the provider has doubts, it may consult a medical adviser or the applicant's doctor, with the applicant's consent.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 9.5
notes: Pleegzorg.nl says a medical statement is rarely needed, for example when a disability might stop a carer offering a safe home. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: A foster child should preferably have a room of their own. This matters less for weekend care.
Jarabee asks for a spare bedroom, along with being 21 and having a stable situation.
notes: Provider practice in Twente, not a national rule.

rule_summary: Foster care is organised by region. People apply to a provider in their own region, found by postcode on pleegzorg.nl.
notes: Most regions have more than one provider.

rule_summary: The right to the foster care allowance ends if the foster family moves abroad.

Every foster carer needs a certificate of no objection (verklaring van geen bezwaar, VGB) from the Child Protection Board (Raad voor de Kinderbescherming). So does everyone aged 12 or over registered at the carer's address.
notes: The value is the age from which people in the household are checked. A new VGB is needed before the first placement, when the carer changes provider, when new people move in, and after 2 years without fostering.

rule_summary: For the VGB the Board checks the population register, its own records and the criminal records system (Justitieel Documentatie Systeem). It also checks partners who live elsewhere. Everyone checked gives written consent.
notes: If something raises doubts, the Board invites the applicant to a talk. A refusal gives reasons and can be challenged.

rule_summary: The Board refuses a VGB in principle after a conviction for a sexual offence or child abuse. Past Board involvement with the family, violent or serious property offences and fraud can also count against an applicant.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 2
notes: Without a VGB the preparation and screening stop. Objections follow the General Administrative Law Act (Awb). Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: The Board tells the provider if the applicant asked for a VGB before. With consent, the provider then always contacts the earlier provider. Refusing consent can be a reason to stop the process.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 2
notes: This aims to stop someone found unsuitable by one provider being taken on by another. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: The provider asks for at least 2 references, with the applicant's consent, and contacts every referee. Preferably one knows the applicant through work, for example an employer, family doctor or a teacher of their child.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 9.4
notes: Referees are asked about the six national criteria. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: A foster carer must have completed a preparation and selection programme offered by the provider.

Each provider sets its own preparation programme. It must cover the legal criteria, the six national criteria and any criteria of its own. Carers of a child they already know also prepare, at least on the six criteria.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 8
notes: Sterk Huis names its registration form after STAP, a preparation method. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Preparation training happens in a group with other applicants. Its length differs by provider but is on average a few half-day sessions (dagdelen).
notes: Topics include the background and development of foster children, attachment and working with parents.

rule_summary: Preparation and screening has 6 parts: information pack, information meeting, preparation programme, home visits, report and final registration. At least 2 professionals are involved throughout.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 7
notes: Providers may order or name the parts differently. The process combines self-selection by the applicant and a binding decision by the provider. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Home visits look at the applicant's living situation, surroundings and background. The applicant's own children are spoken to, and a child already living with the family is seen.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 9
notes: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Applicants are assessed on 6 national criteria: openness, working together and sharing parenting with the parents, helping a child see themselves positively, helping a child change behaviour, judging how fostering changes their own life, and offering a safe home.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 3
notes: Providers may turn the criteria into a competence profile. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Before signing the contract and placing a child, the provider judges whether the child can live with this family. It looks at the child's age and needs, the family make-up and how long the placement is likely to last.
Providers may add criteria of their own, for example on social media, substance use or extreme political, religious or other beliefs. They must write these down and tell applicants in time.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, sections 4 and 5
notes: Online information may only be public information and may only start a conversation, not serve as proof. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: The provider makes a written selection decision with a behavioural scientist or other expert involved. Applicants get the decision in writing and in person, with the report. A refusal states which criteria it is based on.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 11
notes: Approved carers join the provider's pool and wait for a match. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: A foster carer cannot also be the person the provider has asked to support foster carers.
Councils and providers must tell foster carers about the independent confidential adviser (vertrouwenspersoon), whose help is free.
notes: The decree under the Youth Act holds no other rules on who can foster.

rule_summary: It usually takes 4 to 7 months from the first step until the first foster child arrives. It can be quicker or slower.
notes: The steps are an information meeting or talk, preparation, screening, matching and a settling-in period.

rule_summary: If a child already lives with the applicants or will soon, the Board checks criminal records and assesses the VGB request on the same day.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 2
notes: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: De Rading says its preparation and registration for foster care cost nothing.
notes: Provider page. We found no national rule on fees for foster carers.

rule_summary: Foster care can be for a child you already know (netwerkpleegzorg) or for a child you do not know (bestandspleegzorg). It can be full time, part time or crisis care.
notes: Part-time care can be some days a week, weekends or holidays.

rule_summary: There are 3 kinds of foster care contract: a provisional contract for carers of a child they know, the standard contract, and a contract for a foster carer who becomes the child's guardian (pleegoudervoogd).
notes: By law (Jeugdwet art. 5.2), support for a guardian is one conversation a year unless the guardian asks for more.

rule_summary: If someone already cares for the child before a contract is signed, the preparation, VGB and suitability conditions can be met within 13 weeks after signing. The provider must decide within those 13 weeks.
notes: The provider must judge that the care is not harmful to the child. Not given as a value because weeks is not an allowed unit.

rule_summary: When parents agree to the placement, carers of a child they know need a youth help decision (jeugdhulpbesluit) from the council before they can become official foster carers.
notes: The child's legal representative applies. The decision can be challenged.

rule_summary: A foster care contract normally runs until the young person turns 21. It can end earlier if a young person aged 18 or over wants to stop.
notes: Pleegzorg.nl says the right to foster care until 21 dates from 1 July 2018.

rule_summary: After 21, foster care with support can continue until age 23 if needed. The allowance continues while foster care continues.
The provider evaluates with the whole foster family at least once a year, including a safety check at home. The foster child is spoken to without the carers.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 12.1
notes: A breakdown of a placement always leads to an evaluation. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: A new VGB is needed when carers have waited more than 2 years, when the household changes or someone new registers at the address, and when they move to another provider.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, sections 12 and 13
notes: The provider may also ask for a new VGB whenever it sees reason. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: The provider may screen carers again after life changes. It always does so when a carer has a new partner, or when carers of a child they knew want to foster other children.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 13
notes: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Carers must offer a home that is physically and emotionally safe. The provider checks safety at the carers' home at least once a year.
legal_citation: Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, section 3
notes: Safety, sexuality and abuse are discussed openly during preparation. Kwaliteitskader voorbereiding en screening in de pleegzorg, version of June 2026. Agreed by all providers in Jeugdzorg Nederland; quality is checked through HKZ certification.

rule_summary: Providers run training and meetings for foster carers, for example on trauma, teenagers, rights and duties, and stress.
notes: We found no rule on a set number of hours.

rule_summary: The provider pays the foster carer an allowance (pleegvergoeding): a basic amount, which can be raised by a supplement or lowered, plus special costs.
legal_citation: Jeugdwet art. 5.3; Regeling Jeugdwet art. 5.1 to 5.3
notes: The basic amount can be lowered while the child is away for a time; actual necessary costs are then paid up to the basic amount.

rule_summary: In 2026 the basic amount for a child aged 0 to 8 is 757 euro a month (24.88 euro a day).
notes: Ages 9 to 11: 767 euro (25.21 a day). 12 to 15: 835 euro (27.45). 16 and 17: 922 euro (30.31). 18 and over: 931 euro (30.62). The allowance is set by day.

rule_summary: In 2027 the basic amount for a child aged 0 to 8 is 781 euro a month (25.68 euro a day).
legal_citation: Regeling Jeugdwet annex 1, as replaced by the regulation of 11 November 2026
notes: Ages 9 to 11: 791 euro (26.02 a day). 12 to 15: 862 euro (28.33). 16 and 17: 951 euro (31.28). 18 and over: 961 euro (31.60). Staatscourant 2026, 40388.

rule_summary: A supplement of 4.96 euro a day is paid for the first 4 weeks of a crisis placement, and for the third and each further foster child.
notes: From 1 January 2027 it is 5.12 euro a day (Staatscourant 2026, 40388).

rule_summary: For a child with an intellectual, sensory or physical disability, the provider can add up to 4.96 euro a day for necessary costs that the basic amount and other schemes do not cover.
notes: From 1 January 2027 the maximum is 5.12 euro a day. Supplements can be combined.

rule_summary: The provider pays special costs (bijzondere kosten) that are necessary, cannot come from the basic amount or supplements, are not covered by another scheme and cannot reasonably be claimed from the parents.
The basic amount and supplements rise each 1 January in line with the consumer price index, measured July to July. For 2027 the rise is 3.2 percent.
notes: Not given as a value because percent is not an allowed unit.

rule_summary: The foster care allowance is not taxed and does not count as income for benefits, personal budgets or rent support.
notes: Carers with a foster contract and allowance cannot also get child benefit for that child (pleegzorg.nl).

rule_summary: Every foster carer with a foster care contract has a right to the allowance. For part-time care it is paid by the day.
notes: How arrival and departure days are counted differs by provider.

rule_summary: To adopt a child born in the Netherlands you must be an adult and at least 18 years older than the child.
notes: Adulthood starts at 18.

rule_summary: Each adopter must be at least 18 years older than the child.
For intercountry adoption, the minister refuses permission in principle (beginseltoestemming) if an applicant is 42 or older when applying, unless there are special circumstances.
legal_citation: Wet opneming buitenlandse kinderen ter adoptie (Wobka) art. 5(5)(b)

rule_summary: For intercountry adoption, permission is refused if the age gap between an applicant and the child is expected to be more than 40 years when the child arrives, unless there are special circumstances.
notes: The minister may set a condition on the child's age to keep within the 40 years.

rule_summary: Permission in principle is not given or renewed beyond the date an applicant turns 46, unless there are special circumstances.
A court can grant an adoption to one person, or to two people together if they have lived together for at least 3 years in a row just before the request.
notes: The same 3 years apply to a partner adopting their partner's child, unless the child was born within the relationship.

rule_summary: For intercountry adoption only a married couple can apply together. A single applicant who is married or has a partner needs the partner's agreement.
notes: Fiom says unmarried and registered partners both go through the whole process, with one named as the applicant and the other as co-carer.

rule_summary: Grandparents cannot adopt their grandchild.
A court grants an adoption only if it is clearly in the child's interest and the child can be expected to have nothing more from their parents as parents.
notes: Other conditions in art. 228 include that the parents do not object (with exceptions) and no longer hold parental authority.

rule_summary: The adopters must have cared for and raised the child for at least 1 year before the adoption.
notes: This does not apply when a child is born within the relationship of the mother and a female partner.

rule_summary: An intercountry adoption usually takes 2 to 6 years in total.
notes: Fiom is the body appointed to give the compulsory information sessions.

rule_summary: Bringing a foreign child into the Netherlands for adoption needs the minister's prior written permission in principle (beginseltoestemming).
notes: The Central Authority in the Ministry of Justice and Security decides, on advice from the Child Protection Board.

rule_summary: Permission in principle lasts 4 years and can be renewed for 4 years at a time, after a further family study.
notes: Renewal must be asked for at least 12 weeks before it ends (art. 4(b)). Having permission does not give a right to a child.

rule_summary: Permission in principle covers one child, or two siblings or closely attached children at the same time. More is possible only in special circumstances.
Before the minister decides, the Child Protection Board studies whether the applicants are suited to raise a foreign child. The report is discussed with them before it is issued.
notes: Fiom says the study is a series of talks about the family situation and the wish and reasons to adopt.

rule_summary: Before the family study, first-time applicants must take general information sessions under the minister's supervision: 6 meetings, the first an introduction.
legal_citation: Wobka art. 5(2); Besluit opneming buitenlandse kinderen ter adoptie art. 6 and 11
notes: Topics include the birth parents, the child's history, loss and grief, attachment, identity and loyalty, and wishes and limits (Fiom).

rule_summary: Applicants pay 1,595 euro for the compulsory information sessions: 210 euro for the introductory meeting and 1,385 euro for the 5 further meetings.
legal_citation: Besluit opneming buitenlandse kinderen ter adoptie art. 6(2); Wobka art. 4(e)
notes: Fees must be paid before the family study starts.

rule_summary: Fiom says the fees of the licensed intermediary for an intercountry adoption range from 12,000 to over 40,000 euro, depending on the country.
notes: A residence permit for the child costs about 950 euro, and converting a foreign adoption 600 to 1,000 euro, per Fiom.

rule_summary: A one-off contribution of 3,700 euro towards intercountry adoption costs applied only to children adopted between 1 January 2009 and 1 January 2013.
notes: No longer applies to new adoptions.

rule_summary: Adoption costs have not been tax-deductible since 1 January 2013.
Intercountry adoption is being phased out. Licensed intermediaries can propose matches until 1 May 2030; procedures without a match stop then. Matched cases can be completed until 18 December 2030.
legal_citation: Afbouwplan interlandelijke adoptie (9 December 2024); bill to replace the Wobka
notes: A bill went to public consultation in January 2026. Once it is law, no one can apply for a new intercountry adoption. After 2030 the Central Authority takes over remaining tasks.

rule_summary: Fiom has taken no new intercountry adoption applications since 21 May 2024. People who still want to apply are referred to the Central Authority, which talks with them about the very small chance of a completed adoption.
notes: While the current law applies, a person who goes ahead still gets a file number and starts the information sessions. The Child Protection Board advises against starting a new intercountry procedure.

rule_summary: Few children born in the Netherlands are placed for adoption, about 15 to 20 a year. At present no one can sign up for adoption of a child born in the Netherlands.
notes: Fiom says the domestic procedure is largely the same as the intercountry one, including permission in principle and preparation.

rule_summary: A child coming from abroad for adoption must be under 6 on arrival, unless the minister allows an exception on request.
